I also planned to search on these topics:

- How Reformed, dispensational and Pentecostal teachers read verses 1–4 (the mountain of the Lord and swords into plowshares). The question is whether these verses describe the church now or a future thousand-year reign of Christ.
- Catholic and Orthodox writers' use of verses 1–3. Early church writers such as Justin Martyr and Irenaeus applied them to the spread of the gospel.
- Prosperity teaching that uses "each man under his own vine and fig tree" (v. 4).
- The "watchtower of the flock" (*Migdal Eder*, v. 8) and its link with Bethlehem.
- The mention of Babylon in verse 10, which matters in modern scholars' debate about when the chapter was written.

If you ask again in a new message, I'll fetch these pages one or two at a time so I stay under the limit. Then I'll write the notes verse by verse, with a URL after each point.
